bounded_statement: Within the visible files, each authorized source item (a distinct ordered k1,k2 pair) contributes two measurements (columns a and b of its single row) that are placed into the two arms of ttest_ind, a procedure that assumes all 24 observations are mutually independent (df=22); thus each of the 12 source items enters the independence-assuming procedure twice.

counterevidence_considered.description: All 12 ordered (k1,k2) pairs are distinct across the staged rows, so there is no row-level duplication of a source item; under a reading where one 'entry' equals one staged row, each unit enters only once.

evidence.description: The task authorizes the ordered (k1,k2) pair as the single source item.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. Treat each distinct ordered `k1`,`k2` pair as one source item; rows carrying the same ordered pair originate from the same source item.

evidence.description: Each source item's row carries two measurements, a and b, which the workflow routes into the left and right samples of ttest_ind respectively.

source_refs.quoted_text:
left = [float(row["a"]) for row in staged]
right = [float(row["b"]) for row in staged]
result = ttest_ind(left, right)

evidence.description: The reported df=22 = 12 + 12 - 2 confirms the procedure counted 24 observations from 12 source items as independent.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted the alternative reading that 'entry' is row-level, under which the 12 distinct pairs each enter once and no issue exists. I rejected it because ttest_ind does not operate on rows: it operates on 24 scalar observations and its reported df=22 shows every observation, including the two originating from the same authorized source item, was treated as an independent unit. The dependence between the two entries is authorized by the task itself (both carry the same ordered pair), so the repeated entry of the same unit into the independence-assuming procedure is demonstrable from the visible files. Residual uncertainty is interpretive (granularity of 'entry'), not evidential.

root_cause: The workflow splits the within-item paired measurements a and b of every row across the two samples of an independent-samples t-test instead of using a procedure that accounts for within-item dependence, so each task-defined source item is entered twice into a procedure whose validity assumes each observation comes from an independent unit.
